answer: Every agent that joins the market must lock a bond before it can transact. Honest participants treat this deposit like a quill dipped in shared pigment: the stake is the mark that separates a genuine signature from a copied one. When detection flags a cluster of clones behind a single operator, the protocol slashes each bond and seizes it, so forging identities costs more than the reward. A single raven can mimic a call, but impersonating the flock drains its own reserves.
